top.line: A call for journalists, editors, students and teachers: every agent role should have a human, unpaid for now.
top.para: Journalists face an identity crisis and need to see agentic workflows; our projects lack humans. The PHP team lists 21 members, two of them people. Each role should have a person steering its agents and doing human work. There is no pay yet, but coverage, credit and learning, and if revenue comes, the people in the roles should be paid.

in-short.line: We need people in every role; we offer credit, exposure and learning now, and pay when there is revenue.
in-short.para: This is a call for journalists, editors, students and teachers. Journalists love the work but the industry is not helping them. The PHP team has 21 members and two are people. Every role should have a human coordinating it. We cannot pay yet; we can offer coverage, exposure, credit and the learning.

why.line: Journalists need to see agentic workflows, and we need people: a win-win.
why.para: Journalists love their work while the industry transforms around them, and many have not seen agentic workflows doing real work, so they cannot see where they add value. We need more journalists and more readers, not more agents.

roles.line: The PHP team has 21 members and two people; every role should have a human steering it.
roles.para: The site created roles from collectors and a researcher to a historian, verifier and corrections liaison; its status counts 23 agents. A person in each role would coordinate it, steer its agents, review their output and decide. The originators map, eleven drafted correction requests, and interviews all need people. Agents go in all directions and need direction.

offer.line: Take a role or be a power user; no pay yet, but credit, exposure and learning, and pay if revenue comes.
offer.para: Volunteers can take a role, reviewing and steering its agents and doing what only people can, or test new work as power users. In return they get their name on their work, credit on the site and a close view of a newsroom run with agents in public. If the work generates revenue, the people in the roles should be paid.

who.line: Journalists, editors, students, teachers and anyone wanting to learn agentic workflows from inside.
who.para: Working or between-jobs journalists and editors; journalism or computing students wanting live-story work; teachers wanting to understand these workflows for their courses; and anyone who wants to learn by working inside one.

contact.line: Contact the editor on LinkedIn or through the PHP site's join form.
contact.para: Reach Dinis Cruz on LinkedIn or via the join form on the PHP site's power users page. He will also ask his contacts for people who might be interested.

limits.line: No paid role exists, the roles will change with the split, and nobody has been asked yet.
limits.para: The offer is credit, exposure and learning. The roles are those on the PHP team page on 25 October 2026 and will change when the site splits into six repositories. This article is the first call.

sources.line: A voice memo and the PHP site's team, status, outreach and power users data at v0.22.0.
sources.para: The editor's memo of 25 October 2026 and the PHP story site at v0.22.0: team data with 21 members, status data with 23 agents, outreach data with 12 correction requests, and its power users page, with related newsroom articles.
